title: Does swapping the fractions change the product?
description: One half times one quarter and one quarter times one half are worked out and drawn as rectangles. The two rectangles are the same shape turned round. Keeko raises the doubt that the order must matter.
teaching_notes: One idea: the product of two fractions stays the same when the order is swapped. Watch for students who think order matters in multiplication because it matters in subtraction and division.

video_script.why: A learner sees that swapping the two fractions does not change the product, using a rectangle turned round.
video_script.substitution: the numbers of the book's own check, one half and one quarter
video_script.anchor: a rectangle with sides one half and one quarter, and the same rectangle turned round
video_script.wrong_move: believes the order of the fractions changes the product, as it does for subtraction
video_script.fraction_reading: one half, one quarter, one eighth
maths_rules: a rectangle with sides 1/2 and 1/4 has the same area as one with sides 1/4 and 1/2
video_script.design: One rectangle drawn twice, the second turned a quarter turn, with the same area shaded.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the two products are different, because the fractions come in a different order.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>But the same four numbers are multiplied in both products.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The order of multiplying does not matter, though it does for taking away.
